title: Dedicated meter safety net and customer credit claim workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers on Dedicated capacity have observed occasional post-facto billing adjustments when transient GPU contention or racey meter writes cause temporary overcounting or undercounting of reserved throughput and burst usage. This ticket implements a safety net that: 1) prevents negative balance surprises by applying a runtime soft-stop and negative-balance guard, 2) creates a customer-facing credit claim workflow for manual review and auto-apply heuristics, and 3) adds end-to-end auditability to prove correctness for disputed invoices. The goal is to reduce manual billing escalations, provide deterministic automated corrections, and preserve SLO/throughput guarantees while protecting revenue integrity.
acceptance_criteria: Metering pipeline exposes per-tenant minute-granularity deltas and a correction_reason tag
Runtime soft-stop prevents tenant token balance from going below configured floor without dropping in-flight inference requests abruptly
Automated credit rule: when correction_delta < -0.5% and matches known transient patterns, system auto-applies a provisional credit and creates a ticket for billing ops
Customer console shows a clear "Usage adjustments" timeline entry with link to audit query and optional claim button
End-to-end reconciliation queries (ClickHouse/Snowflake) produce identical totals to event-sourced ledger within a configurable 60-day window
No observable tail-latency regression (>2ms p95) from added meter instrumentation on serving path in canary cluster
technical_notes: Add a per-tenant 'safety_floor' in the billing ledger that is enforced by the throttle controller. When predicted debit would breach floor, mark request as 'soft-limited' and route to best-effort pool rather than hard-drop.
Introduce correction_reason tags: 'write_race', 'shard_lag', 'aggregation_trim', 'manual_adjustment' to ledger events so downstream billing can filter and surface root cause
Implement idempotent event consumer for 'meter_delta' topics to dedupe double-writes from edge aggregators. Use message dedupe key = tenant_id + window_start + producer_instance
Store minute-level raw_deltas in a separate time-series shard (usage_shards) for 90 days and derive hourly/tenant rollups asynchronously for queries
Develop a small 'claims' service: POST /claims creates review ticket, attaches implicated ledger events and debug traces, and can trigger auto-credit if matched to heuristics
Add a canary flag that turns on correction auto-apply only for internal tenants and opt-in customers during rollout
Define end-to-end audit query and materialized view in ClickHouse: 'billing_audits.v_meter_rollups' with columns tenant, window_start, raw_sum, ledger_sum, corrections_sum
tasks: Design data model for usage_shards and safety_floor (backend) - Marco
Implement idempotent consumer for meter_delta stream - Jin
Modify throttle controller to consult safety_floor and mark soft-limited requests - Priya
Build claims service and minimal UI hook in Console - Sofia
Add correction_reason tagging at aggregator stage - Marco
Create ClickHouse materialized view + test queries and dashboards - Analytics
E2E tests that simulate racey writes across 3 aggregators and assert final ledger invariants - QA
Run canary on internal dedicated cluster and collect perf signals for 2 weeks - SRE
decisions: We will prefer soft-throttling + best-effort routing over outright request rejection to avoid user-visible errors during transient metering anomalies
Correction heuristics will be conservative: auto-credit only when delta qualifies on multiple signals (pattern, magnitude, and matching edge traces)
Event dedupe will be implemented at consumer level instead of changing producer semantics to minimize rollout blast radius
We'll maintain raw minute-granularity deltas for 90 days to enable fast audits while keeping long-term rollups for billing history
